definition.description:
JavaScript async body or arrow with read, write, edit, bash; file:path runs a program file. Put text/scripts/argv in data (default ≤48000 serialized JSON characters). No fs/import/require.

read(path|paths, offset?, limit?) → raw text/text[]; directories → entries[]
Path-only: ≤160 lines AND ≤8192 characters; otherwise read(path,{offset:1,limit:80}), read(path,{about:"keywords"}), or read(path,{complete:true}). Offsets are 1-based; complete requires the whole file within the default 31744-character budget. Large JSONL: bounded parser via bash.
read(imagePath) → image (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP); ≤16 attachments / 20 MiB total, otherwise failure
read({path,json:selector}) → parsed JSON; selectors: ".field", ".items[0:3]", ".items.length", quoted keys, true. 16 MiB cap; no jq.
Oversized JSON → {status:"too_large",path,keys} (arrays: length); narrow the selector.
read("symbol or question") → same view as resolve:true
read({query,resolve:true}) → {status,path,line,text,...}; check status
read(path,{about}) → matching windows; read({query,evidence:true}) → ranked evidence; read({path,outline:true}) → declarations
write(path,text) → replace unread workspace file; write({path,content,append:true}) → append without reading. After read use edit; replace:true overrides.
edit(path,oldText,newText) | edit({path,edits:[{oldText,newText}]}) → numbered post-edit lines, checks, references. oldText must match read() exactly; misses return numbered windows.
Found is a span, not the file. edit(view,text) replaces the window; edit(view,old,new) requires a unique match within it.
edit(async()=>{...}) → checkpoint: merge on success; rollback/rethrow on failure; catch to recover
bash(command,{cwd?,timeoutMs?}) or bash({command,args}) for literal argv → bounded output; nonzero throws; inherits program timeoutMs unless overridden

Array reads reject failures; use Promise.allSettled for optional paths. Edits stage until success; bash commits preceding writes. Batch known reads/edits/tests with Promise.all or programs.
programs:[{code|file,data?},...] runs sequential fresh guests with separate commits; top-level data defaults per entry. Failure stops, keeping earlier commits. parallel:true runs disjoint entries concurrently. Separate calls only for new model decisions.

data.introduction:
The model submits JavaScript, not four separately advertised native tools.
Ordinary JavaScript control flow remains available; the guest command bindings
are only `read`, `edit`, `write`, and `bash`. Supernova supplies retrieval,
transactional file operations, batching, bounded results and the grouped nova UI.
